leaf: rmcp-v3.1.4 tasks/cancel authenticated-owner gate and stock acknowledgement surface
result: Exact modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk@4a738b9dd99eaca418b614afa433a0cbdaf8d056 resolves the stock tasks/cancel seam. Service<RoleServer>::handle_request first calls validate_tasks_capability::<CancelTaskMethod,_>, then invokes ServerHandler::cancel_task(request.params, context), and maps successful Result<(),McpError> through ServerResult::task_ack. The trait method is cancel_task(&self, CancelTaskParams, RequestContext<RoleServer>) -> Future<Result<(),McpError>>; its stock default ignores request/context and returns McpError::method_not_found::<CancelTaskMethod>(). CancelTaskParams is non_exhaustive and contains meta: Option<RequestMetaObject> plus public task_id: String, with new(task_id) setting meta=None. ServerResult::task_ack converts () into TaskAckResult::new(), i.e. the standard empty tasks/update/tasks/cancel acknowledgement carrying the SEP-2322 resultType=complete discriminator. Therefore the smallest application-owned fail-closed cancellation owner gate can extract request.task_id, derive the authenticated principal from trusted RequestContext transport metadata as already established in this role's source chain, look up application-owned persistent {task_id -> owner_principal_id,...}, map both missing task_id and owner mismatch to the identical McpError::invalid_params constant message/data=None before invoking any cancellation mutation, and return Ok(()) only after an owner-authorized cooperative cancellation request is accepted. This prevents task-existence leakage across those two cases at the handler error surface, but is an application-level deduction, not stock rmcp authorization/persistence behavior; it does not prove cancellation completion, because the exact handler comment states observable task status may lag after the empty acknowledgement.
